parallel_group.prompt:
In KBUtilLib, create a new subpackage under the KBase domain named 'berdl' and implement its three pure-logic modules with unit tests. Read agent-io/prds/berdl-lakehouse-skills/fullprompt.md first — it is authoritative.

1) naming.py — normalization for BERDL database names. The platform is in a dual-read window: the database list returns BOTH Iceberg-style dotted names and legacy Delta-style underscored names, and the SAME logical dataset appears under both (e.g. 'aiale.dataset1' and 'aiale_dataset1'; 'kbaseincubator.fitness' and 'kbaseincubator_fitness'). Implement: pairing of dotted/underscored forms of the same logical dataset; deduplication that PREFERS the dotted (Iceberg) form; marking of the underscored form as legacy rather than hiding it (never present the two as unrelated datasets); and bidirectional translation of the personal-catalog alias, which is 'my' in Spark and '{username}' in Trino.

2) membership.py — decode tenant permission level. get_my_groups() returns a FLAT list in which read-only membership is encoded as a NAME SUFFIX, not a structured field: 'enigmaro' means read-only on 'enigma'. The safe decode is: strip a trailing 'ro' and test whether the remainder appears in the available-groups list. A naive endswith('ro') check is WRONG and must not be used — it would misclassify any tenant whose real name ends in those letters. Return a mapping of {tenant: 'rw'|'ro'}.

3) tokens.py — token resolution with a FIXED precedence: KBASE_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable FIRST, then ~/.kbase/token, then config. This ordering fixes a verified bug: the existing KBBERDLUtils reads only ~/.kbase/token and raises 'No KBase token available' even in-pod where KBASE_AUTH_TOKEN is set and works. A token value must NEVER be logged, printed, returned in a repr, or written to any artifact.

Write unit tests for all three. Tests must be pure — no network, no live BERDL, no pod dependency — so they run in ordinary CI. Test external behavior (given this input, is the decision right), not internal call sequences. Include an explicit membership test for a tenant whose real name ends in the suffix letters and must NOT be misclassified, and an explicit tokens test asserting no token value appears in output. Do not create transports.py or capability.py in this task. Follow the repo's existing module and test conventions.
parallel_group.success_criteria: A 'berdl' subpackage exists under the KBase domain of KBUtilLib containing naming.py, membership.py and tokens.py plus a test module for each. The full test suite passes. The tests demonstrably cover: dotted/underscored pairing and dedup preferring the dotted form; legacy marking; my/{username} alias translation in both directions; ro-suffix decoding INCLUDING a negative case where a tenant name legitimately ends in those letters and is not misclassified; and token precedence env -> file -> config with an assertion that no token value is emitted in output. No network calls occur during the test run.

parallel_group.prompt:
In the KBUtilLib 'berdl' subpackage created in the previous phase, implement transports.py with two transports behind a common interface. Read agent-io/prds/berdl-lakehouse-skills/fullprompt.md first — its verified import map is authoritative and must be followed exactly.

InPodTransport wraps the pod-only package berdl_notebook_utils. CRITICAL: the published BERDL guides write every helper call bare, claiming functions are 'auto-imported, no imports needed'. That is TRUE ONLY inside a notebook kernel where startup.py injects the names. Code running in a terminal or subprocess gets ImportError. Use these exact import paths: 'berdl_notebook_utils' top level for get_spark_session, create_namespace_if_not_exists, get_databases, get_tables, get_table_schema, get_db_structure, get_trino_connection, refresh_spark_environment, table_exists, remove_table, get_minio_client, get_s3_client, and the tenancy/steward functions; 'berdl_notebook_utils.governance' for get_my_groups, get_my_workspace, get_credentials, request_tenant_access, list_available_groups, list_namespace_access, grant_namespace_access, revoke_namespace_access, get_tenant_stewards and the admin operations; 'berdl_notebook_utils.spark' for start_spark_connect_server, stop_spark_connect_server, get_spark_connect_status; 'berdl_notebook_utils.refresh' for refresh_spark_environment and rotate_credentials.

OffPodTransport is a pure-requests REST client, read-only BY CONSTRUCTION — it must expose no write method at all. It MUST NOT import berdl_notebook_utils at module scope, because that package does not exist off-pod and a module-scope import would break every off-pod import of this subpackage. It uses tokens.py for credentials and may reuse the existing KBBERDLUtils REST client internally. Known limitation to document in the code: the REST surface returns tenant catalogs only — the personal catalog does not appear — so off-pod discovery of personal tables must not be promised.

Both transports normalize database names through naming.py rather than returning raw platform output. Do not implement BerdlCapability in this task. No tests are required for transports (they need live BERDL); verification is by hand against the pod.
parallel_group.success_criteria: transports.py exists in the berdl subpackage defining InPodTransport and OffPodTransport behind a common interface. Importing the berdl subpackage succeeds on a machine where berdl_notebook_utils is NOT installed, proving no module-scope import of the pod-only package. OffPodTransport exposes no write method. Every berdl_notebook_utils helper is referenced via the submodule path given in the PRD import map, with no bare notebook-style call. Both transports route database names through naming.py. The existing test suite still passes.

parallel_group.prompt:
In the KBUtilLib 'berdl' subpackage, implement capability.py defining BerdlCapability — the deep module — plus unit tests for its pure logic. Read agent-io/prds/berdl-lakehouse-skills/fullprompt.md first; it is authoritative.

Interface: locus() -> 'in_pod'|'off_pod'; databases() -> normalized deduplicated list; memberships() -> {tenant: 'rw'|'ro'}; load(...) -> in-pod only; query(sql) -> routed by locus and intent.

locus() must test IMPORTABILITY of berdl_notebook_utils, not only environment variables, because the variables alone do not guarantee the package is present. Select the transport from the detected locus.

load() routes all writes through data_lakehouse_ingest.ingest — never raw writeTo — because ingest applies schema enforcement in both source modes. Signature is ingest(config, spark=None, logger=None, minio_client=None, dataframes=None). Support BOTH source modes, selected by input type: DataFrame mode passes frames via dataframes= keyed by table name, which short-circuits the bronze read entirely so NO MinIO staging is needed and the 'paths' config section MUST be omitted; bronze mode reads files and requires paths.bronze_base plus per-table bronze_path/format. Config may be an inline dict — no file staging. Config schema: required top-level 'dataset' and 'tables'; optional 'tenant', 'is_tenant', 'pipeline_name', 'paths', 'defaults'; each table requires 'name', optional 'comment', 'schema_sql' or 'schema', 'enabled', 'bronze_path', 'format'.

Write semantics that MUST be handled: mode is only 'overwrite' or 'append'; APPEND TO A NON-EXISTENT TABLE RAISES ValueError, so the loader must detect table existence and choose overwrite for first creation so a re-runnable load does not fail on first execution; overwrite maps to createOrReplace, a full destructive replace recoverable only via Iceberg snapshot time travel; partition_by accepts a string or a list.

Preflight, BEFORE staging or writing anything: resolve locus; refuse off-pod; confirm READ-WRITE membership on the target tenant via membership.py; report whether the target table exists and whether the operation will create, append or replace. Postflight: verify by row count and by reading snapshot history, and report the new snapshot.

Off-pod, load() must raise with the reason (writes need a Spark session, which exists only in the pod), the target machine (kbhub), and the exact command to run there. It must NOT stage data, generate artifacts, or dispatch work.

Tests are pure-logic only, no network: ingest-config construction for both source modes (assert DataFrame mode omits 'paths' and bronze mode includes it); create-vs-append mode selection given table existence; and off-pod load() raising with actionable guidance. Do not write tests requiring live BERDL.
parallel_group.success_criteria: capability.py defines BerdlCapability exposing locus, databases, memberships, load and query. Unit tests pass and cover: ingest-config construction in DataFrame mode omitting 'paths' and in bronze mode including paths.bronze_base; selection of overwrite rather than append when the target table does not exist; and off-pod load() raising an error whose message names the pod requirement, the kbhub machine, and a concrete command. locus() is shown to test importability of berdl_notebook_utils rather than environment variables alone. No write path bypasses data_lakehouse_ingest.ingest. Tests make no network calls and the full suite passes.

parallel_group.prompt:
Author the 'berdl-session' skill as a markdown file in KBUtilLib's agent-io/skills/ directory, following the frontmatter and structure conventions of the six skills KBUtilLib already hosts there. Read agent-io/prds/berdl-lakehouse-skills/fullprompt.md first; it is authoritative.

This is the foundation skill the other three depend on. It must encode:

1) THE IMPORT MAP — the highest-value fact. The BERDL guides claim helpers are auto-imported with no imports needed; that holds ONLY in a notebook kernel. A skill in a terminal gets ImportError on its first call. Reproduce the PRD's verified import map in full (top-level berdl_notebook_utils, .governance, .spark, .refresh, and data_lakehouse_ingest).

2) LOCUS DETECTION — in-pod versus off-pod, tested by importability of berdl_notebook_utils rather than environment variables alone.

3) THE CREDENTIAL ESCALATION LADDER, in order, and explain WHY the order matters: (a) NON-ROTATING FIRST — get_credentials() then start_spark_connect_server(force_restart=True), then a fresh session; this re-fetches current credentials WITHOUT rotating them so it cannot invalidate credentials in use elsewhere; (b) kernel restart if catalogs are still missing; (c) ROTATING — refresh_spark_environment(), which rotates S3 and Polaris credentials and WILL BREAK other kernels, running scripts and remote connections using the old ones, so it is never the first move; (d) server restart then browser refresh; (e) escalate to the BERDL platform team.

4) THE ACCESS-DENIAL TAXONOMY — classify BEFORE fixing. These are EXPECTED ISOLATION and must NOT trigger a credential fix: AccessDenied on a prefix spanning multiple tenants or users; AccessDenied listing the Spark job-logs bucket, which is write-only for users; and a prefix listing returning more than expected because 'aws s3 ls' does no implicit trailing-slash matching, so a query for 'kbase' also matches 'kbaseincubator' — this affects both initial target tenants directly. Genuine credential drift looks different: the tenant browser never renders, favorites are empty, the UI lags, or reads and writes return 403 on paths the user does hold. Misreading expected isolation as breakage leads directly to the damaging rotating fix.

5) THE VIRTUALENV AND KERNEL PROCEDURE, including the pip hazard: running pip install outside an activated venv silently falls back to a --user install into ~/.local, which shadows the base image for the entire server, breaks the file browser and Spark, and SURVIVES RESTARTS. Include the recovery.

The skill should call into the BerdlCapability layer rather than reimplementing logic. Do not modify any Python module in this task.
parallel_group.success_criteria: A berdl-session skill markdown file exists in KBUtilLib's agent-io/skills/ with frontmatter matching the conventions of the skills already there. Its body contains the complete verified import map covering all four import paths; locus detection specified as an importability test; the five-step credential ladder in the correct order with an explicit statement that the rotating fix breaks other live sessions and is never first; the access-denial taxonomy distinguishing expected isolation from genuine drift and naming the kbase/kbaseincubator trailing-slash case; and the venv/kernel procedure including the pip --user shadowing hazard and its recovery. No Python module is modified.

parallel_group.prompt:
Author the 'berdl-load' skill as a markdown file in KBUtilLib's agent-io/skills/, following the conventions of the skills already hosted there. Read agent-io/prds/berdl-lakehouse-skills/fullprompt.md first; it is authoritative.

This skill is IN-POD ONLY — writes require a Spark session that exists only in the BERDL JupyterHub pod. It must encode:

1) PREFLIGHT, before staging or writing anything: resolve locus and refuse off-pod with the reason, the target machine (kbhub), and the exact command to run there — never stage data, generate artifacts, or dispatch work off-pod. Confirm READ-WRITE membership on the target tenant, because read-only and read-write are DIFFERENT GROUPS and discovering read-only mid-load means a Slack approval cycle measured in hours, not a retry. Report whether the target table exists and whether the operation will create, append, or replace.

2) SOURCE-MODE ROUTING — both modes are first-class, selected by input type. DataFrame mode passes frames via ingest(dataframes=...) keyed by table name, short-circuiting the bronze read so no MinIO staging occurs and the 'paths' config section is omitted; this is the default when a DataFrame is in hand. Bronze mode reads CSV/TSV/JSON/XML/Parquet files and requires paths.bronze_base plus per-table bronze_path/format. All writes go through data_lakehouse_ingest.ingest, never raw writeTo, because ingest applies schema enforcement in both modes.

3) WRITE SEMANTICS: mode is only overwrite or append; APPEND TO A NON-EXISTENT TABLE RAISES ValueError so first creation must use overwrite; overwrite maps to createOrReplace, a full destructive replace recoverable only via Iceberg snapshot time travel; partition_by takes a string or list.

4) POSTFLIGHT VERIFICATION — confirm by row count and by reading snapshot history, and report the new snapshot. Success is verified, not assumed.

5) NAMESPACE LIFECYCLE, including teardown. Iceberg via Polaris REST does NOT support CASCADE. Teardown is: enumerate tables (requesting a Python list, not the default JSON string), DROP TABLE ... PURGE each, then DROP NAMESPACE. Omitting PURGE silently ORPHANS the S3 data files. Teardown is irreversible: require explicit confirmation and display exactly what will be deleted first. Also cover Iceberg schema evolution (add, rename, drop column without rewriting data).

Note the initial targets are the aiale and kbaseincubator tenants, on both of which read-write access is already held. The skill calls into BerdlCapability rather than reimplementing logic. Do not modify any Python module in this task.
parallel_group.success_criteria: A berdl-load skill markdown file exists in KBUtilLib's agent-io/skills/ with conforming frontmatter. Its body specifies: an off-pod refusal that names the pod requirement, kbhub, and a concrete command, and that explicitly forbids staging or dispatching; a read-write membership precondition checked before staging, with the async Slack approval consequence stated; both source modes with DataFrame mode omitting 'paths' and bronze mode requiring bronze_base; the rule that append to a non-existent table raises and first creation must use overwrite; that overwrite is a destructive full replace; postflight verification by row count and snapshot; and the purge-ordered teardown with an explicit warning that omitting PURGE orphans S3 files and that teardown requires confirmation. No Python module is modified.

parallel_group.prompt:
Author the 'berdl-query' skill as a markdown file in KBUtilLib's agent-io/skills/, following the conventions of the skills already hosted there. Read agent-io/prds/berdl-lakehouse-skills/fullprompt.md first; it is authoritative.

This skill works in BOTH loci. It must encode:

1) ENGINE ROUTING — Trino for interactive reads and cross-catalog joins; it is READ-ONLY BY DESIGN and rejects INSERT, CREATE, DROP and every other write. Spark for heavy ETL and anything that writes. REST/MCP off-pod.

2) THE ALIAS TRAP — the personal-catalog alias 'my' is SPARK-ONLY. Trino requires '{username}'. A query written for one engine silently fails on the other. Translation must go through the naming layer, not be done ad hoc at call sites.

3) THE DUAL-NAME PROBLEM — the platform is in a dual-read window and the database list returns BOTH Iceberg-style dotted names and legacy Delta-style underscored names, with the SAME logical dataset appearing under both (aiale.dataset1 and aiale_dataset1; kbaseincubator.fitness and kbaseincubator_fitness). Name alone does not disambiguate. Prefer the dotted Iceberg form; mark the underscored form as legacy rather than hiding it; and NEVER present the two as unrelated datasets.

4) DISCOVERY — listing databases, tables and schemas, and the Trino discovery statements including information_schema.

5) CROSS-CATALOG JOINS between the personal catalog and tenant catalogs in a single query.

6) TIME TRAVEL AND SNAPSHOT INSPECTION — Iceberg-only: reading a table as of a snapshot id or timestamp, and inspecting the .snapshots, .history and .files metadata tables. Time travel is the recovery path after a destructive overwrite.

7) OFF-POD LIMITATION, stated honestly — the REST surface returns tenant catalogs only; the personal catalog does not appear, so off-pod discovery of personal tables must not be promised. Also note that off-pod has not yet been proven end to end: the REST route authenticates and needs no SSH tunnel, but off-pod token resolution is unverified on a real off-pod machine.

The skill calls into BerdlCapability rather than reimplementing logic. Do not modify any Python module in this task.
parallel_group.success_criteria: A berdl-query skill markdown file exists in KBUtilLib's agent-io/skills/ with conforming frontmatter. Its body specifies: Trino-versus-Spark routing with Trino stated as read-only and rejecting writes; the my/{username} alias trap with translation routed through the naming layer; the dual dotted/underscored name problem with the rule to prefer dotted, mark underscored as legacy, and never present them as unrelated; discovery commands for both engines; cross-catalog joins; Iceberg time travel and snapshot/history/files inspection identified as the post-overwrite recovery path; and an explicit statement that the off-pod REST surface exposes tenant catalogs only and is not yet proven end to end. No Python module is modified.

parallel_group.prompt:
Author the 'berdl-tenant' skill as a markdown file in KBUtilLib's agent-io/skills/, following the conventions of the skills already hosted there. Read agent-io/prds/berdl-lakehouse-skills/fullprompt.md first; it is authoritative.

This skill works in BOTH loci. It must encode:

1) MEMBERSHIP DECODING — get_my_groups() returns a FLAT list where read-only is encoded as a NAME SUFFIX, not a structured field: 'enigmaro' means read-only on 'enigma'. The safe decode strips a trailing 'ro' and tests the remainder against the available-groups list; a naive endswith('ro') check is wrong. Report permission level per tenant, since read-write is the precondition for any load.

2) ACCESS REQUESTS — requesting tenant access is an ASYNCHRONOUS HUMAN APPROVAL STEP via Slack, typically same-day during business hours. Set that expectation explicitly and do NOT poll for approval.

3) SHARING DOCTRINE — the share_table, unshare_table, make_table_public and make_table_private family is DEPRECATED and MUST NOT be emitted. A model trained on older documentation will reach for these functions, so the skill must actively steer away from them. Sharing is achieved by creating in a tenant catalog, and refined with namespace ACLs.

4) NAMESPACE ACLS AND STEWARDSHIP — these exist in the installed package but appear in NONE of the published guides, so they must be documented here. Inspection is ALWAYS available: list_namespace_access, get_tenant_stewards, get_tenant_members, list_tenants, get_my_groups, show_my_tenants. MUTATION REQUIRES EXPLICIT CONFIRMATION: grant_namespace_access, revoke_namespace_access, assign_steward, remove_steward, add_tenant_member, remove_tenant_member. Access changes on shared tenants are hard to notice and hard to reverse, which is why they are gated.

5) ADMIN OPERATIONS — these require the CDM_JUPYTERHUB_ADMIN role granted via the KBase Auth Server, and fail with an authentication error without it. Note the tenancy v2 API (list_tenants, get_tenant_detail, get_tenant_members, add_tenant_member, update_tenant_metadata) supersedes create_tenant_and_assign_users.

6) PRIVACY — AI-ALE holds collaborator material. BERDL's own documentation warns that query results routed through the MCP server reach external servers. Treat tenant contents with the same care as other sensitive project material: do not route them through external services, renderers, or pastebins.

Use the correct submodule import paths from the PRD import map — most of these functions live in berdl_notebook_utils.governance, not at top level. The skill calls into BerdlCapability rather than reimplementing logic. Do not modify any Python module in this task.
parallel_group.success_criteria: A berdl-tenant skill markdown file exists in KBUtilLib's agent-io/skills/ with conforming frontmatter. Its body specifies: the ro-suffix membership decode with the naive endswith check explicitly rejected; access requests described as an asynchronous human Slack approval with no polling; the deprecated sharing family named and forbidden, with tenant catalogs plus namespace ACLs given as the replacement; the always-available inspection operations separated from the mutation operations that require explicit confirmation; the CDM_JUPYTERHUB_ADMIN requirement for admin operations; and the privacy constraint on routing tenant contents to external services. All governance functions are referenced via the berdl_notebook_utils.governance path rather than as bare or top-level calls. No Python module is modified.
